A.explanation: The joule is energy or work, $W = Fs$, so $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2} \times 1 \text{ m} = 1 \text{ kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-2}$.

B.explanation: The newton is force, $F = ma$, so $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$, which has only $\text{m}^{1}$ not $\text{m}^{2}$.

C.explanation: The pascal is pressure, $p = F/A$, so $1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$, which is different in both $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$ powers.

D.explanation: The watt is power, $P = E/t$, so $1 \text{ W} = 1 \text{ J s}^{-1} = 1 \text{ kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-3}$, with $\text{s}^{-3}$ not $\text{s}^{-2}$.

Recall that work and energy come from $force \times distance$ and force itself is $mass \times acceleration$ with unit $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$.
Expand each named unit - joule, newton, pascal, watt - into $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$ using $W = Fs$, $p = F/A$ and $P = W/t$, then match the powers of $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$.
walkthrough: Identify the target: find the named unit whose definition reduces to $\text{kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-2}$ in SI base units.
Use the defining relations: force is $F = ma$, work or energy is $W = Fs$, pressure is $p = F/A$, power is $P = W/t$.

Build up the joule: $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg} \times 1 \text{ m s}^{-2} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$, then multiply by distance for energy, $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N} \times 1 \text{ m} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2} \times 1 \text{ m}$.
Simplify to $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-2}$, which exactly matches the question, with correct units throughout.
Check the others: newton gives $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, pascal gives $\text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$, watt gives $\text{kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-3}$, so none matches.
Therefore the joule matches the given base-unit combination. This is option A
